author: kirubaharan181
description: Use when scope is needed before design: elicits, documents, validates requirements and UX. Do NOT use for architecture or coding.
purpose: Converts agreed business goals into requirements that are testable, traced and validated, plus the user-experience artifacts that show how they will be met. It owns stages 11-22: elicitation, documentation, functional and non-functional requirements, research, journeys, wireframes, UI and UX, prototypes, accessibility review and validation.
when_to_use: Stakeholder needs must be captured as requirements with acceptance criteria.
User research, journeys, wireframes or prototypes are needed before build.
Accessibility or non-functional targets must be stated and made measurable.
when_not_to_use: Deciding system structure or technology: use technical-architecture.
Testing the built UI: use quality-assurance.
prerequisites: An approved goal or business case, or an explicit statement that none exists.
Access to stakeholders or their recorded input.
A requirement identifier scheme; create one if none exists.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: requirements with unique ids, sources and acceptance criteria
validated requirements baseline approved by the product owner

decision_rules.situation: Requirement uses vague words (fast, easy, robust)
decision_rules.action: Rewrite with a measure and condition before baselining.
Log the conflict and send it to the product owner; do not pick silently.

decision_rules.situation: A requirement has no source need

decision_rules.action: Default to the organization's stated standard and level, and record the assumption.

quality_gates: Each requirement is unique, testable and traced to a need
Non-functional targets have numbers and a verification method
Key states (empty, loading, error) are designed

examples.title: Make a vague requirement testable
examples.request: Rewrite the requirement 'the report should be fast'.
examples.context: Reports show up to 10,000 rows; support complains about waiting.
examples.behavior: Ask for the target audience and load, then express it with a percentile and condition and add an acceptance example.
examples.output: REQ-014: Reports of up to 10,000 rows display within 3 seconds at the 95th percentile. Acceptance: load a 10,000-row report in the test environment and measure.
examples.acceptance: The requirement names a measure, condition and a way to test it.

examples.title: Resolve conflicting stakeholder needs
examples.request: Sales wants a one-click export; security wants approval for every export.
examples.behavior: Record both needs with sources, propose options (role-based approval, limited fields), and route the decision to the product owner.
examples.output: Conflict log entry with options and a pending decision.
examples.acceptance: The conflict is logged and escalated, not silently resolved.

limitations: Cannot know what users want without research or recorded input; it will not invent personas or quotes.
Does not approve the baseline: the product owner does.
Design artifacts are not tested on real users unless a test is run and recorded.

troubleshooting.cause: No access to the people who know the need
troubleshooting.resolution: State the gap, mark affected requirements as unvalidated, and schedule the sessions.
Baseline the set and route changes through a recorded request with impact.
Ask for the standard and level; record the assumption if none is given.

handoffs.artifact: wireframes, UI designs and acceptance criteria
acceptance criteria and risk list for test design
